evals.prompt: I'm the product designer on 'Lumen', a subscription budgeting app. I've finished the redesign of our payment-method screen in Figma: a card list, an 'Add payment method' form (card number, expiry, CVC with inline validation), a primary 'Save card' button, and a confirmation toast. It ships on web (desktop + mobile breakpoints) next sprint under ticket LUM-482, and two frontend engineers are implementing it. Prepare the complete developer handoff package for this screen: everything they need — files, tokens, states, assets, accessibility — so they never have to guess.
evals.expected_output: A complete handoff package: organized source-file structure, breakpoint-specific guidance for desktop and mobile, design tokens in [category]-[variant]-[state] form with matching CSS variables and a DTCG JSON export, exported assets, a full component-state matrix (default/hover/focus/active/disabled plus loading for the async save, error for validation, success for the toast), accessibility notes (semantics, focus order, contrast, labels), a link to LUM-482, and a workflow that includes an implementation walkthrough and design QA before release.
expectations: All required artifacts are present: organized source design files, responsive/breakpoint guidance, design tokens, exported assets, interaction states, accessibility notes, and a reference to ticket LUM-482
Design tokens follow the [category]-[variant]-[state] naming structure with matching CSS variable forms (e.g. color-primary-500 / --color-primary-500)
Token names are semantic for intent (e.g. color-error-default), not raw values (not color-red-500), and are stated to be identical in Figma and code
Tokens are exported (or specified for export) as JSON in the Design Tokens Community Group format for automated import
The 'Save card' button and form fields document all five always-required states: default, hover, keyboard focus (with visible focus ring), active/pressed, and disabled

Conditional states are covered because they apply here: loading (async save), error (inline validation with label/color/icon), and success (confirmation toast); empty state is addressed for the card list
Accessibility notes cover semantics, focus behavior, contrast, input labels, and alt text where applicable — as part of the package, not deferred
Both mobile and desktop behavior are addressed with breakpoint-specific mocks or guidance
The handoff plan includes a walkthrough with the implementing engineers, a channel for follow-up questions, and design QA before release

evals.prompt: Our agency designer left last week. All we have is a single flat Figma page called 'Dashboard v7 FINAL' with the desktop mockups — no styles library, no named layers, nothing else — and the client wants us to 'just send the devs whatever they need' by Friday. Put together the dev handoff from this.
evals.expected_output: A response that inventories what a complete handoff requires against what actually exists, and explicitly flags the gaps — no design tokens, no responsive/mobile mocks, no documented interaction states, no exported assets, no accessibility notes, no ticket/scope references, and no engineer involvement to date — proposing a remediation plan and asking targeted questions rather than fabricating token values, breakpoints, or states the design never defined.
expectations: The response does not fabricate token values, breakpoints, or component states that the file does not define; gaps are flagged, not silently filled
It flags the absence of design tokens for typography, color, spacing, and motion, and proposes deriving/confirming them rather than inventing them
It flags that only desktop mocks exist — responsive guidance or mobile/breakpoint mocks are a required artifact and currently missing
It flags that interaction states (hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, empty, error) are undocumented and each interactive component needs them before handoff
It flags missing accessibility notes (semantics, focus, contrast, labels, alt text) as a required artifact, not a follow-up task
It flags that no tickets/stories/implementation scope are referenced and asks what the engineering scope is
It flags that engineers were never involved pre-freeze and calls for a feasibility/component-reuse review with them before treating the design as final
It asks concrete clarifying questions (or lists required inputs and owners) instead of delivering a package that pretends to be complete

evals.prompt:
Review this handoff note our designer posted before going on leave, and list every problem with it as a handoff:

--- HANDOFF: Settings redesign ---
Figma: [link] (design is final and frozen — we didn't loop in the engineers, but it's pixel-perfect so it should be fine)
Tokens: main blue is 'Brand/Blue/Primary' in Figma; in code please use --color-blue-500. Error text is 'color-red-500'.
Button spec: default and hover states are in the file. That should cover it.
Accessibility: we'll do an a11y pass after launch if there's time.
Process: this is the final drop — I'm out for 3 weeks, any questions can wait until I'm back. No design QA needed since the mockups are exact.
evals.expected_output: A review that catches every planted defect: mismatched token naming between Figma and code plus value-based instead of semantic names; button states missing keyboard focus, active, and disabled (and any loading/error states); accessibility deferred to post-launch instead of shipped as a required artifact; design frozen with zero engineer involvement or feasibility review; handoff treated as a one-time drop with no support channel or update notifications; and design QA skipped — each mapped to the skill's fix.
expectations: Flags the Figma-vs-code token name mismatch ('Brand/Blue/Primary' vs '--color-blue-500') — names must be identical in design tool and code
Flags 'color-red-500' and '--color-blue-500' as value-based names and requires semantic intent names (e.g. color-error-default, color-primary-500)
Flags the button spec as incomplete: keyboard focus (with visible focus ring), active/pressed, and disabled states are always required beyond default and hover
Flags 'a11y pass after launch if there's time' — accessibility notes are a required handoff artifact, not an afterthought
Flags that the design was frozen without engineer involvement or a pre-handoff feasibility/component-reuse review

Flags the 'final drop, questions wait 3 weeks' stance as the one-time-drop anti-pattern — handoff requires async implementation support, a designated follow-up contact, and explicit update notifications if specs change
Flags 'no design QA needed' — design QA before release is a required workflow step regardless of mockup fidelity
Each finding is paired with the concrete corrective action from the skill, not just a complaint
